title: RSI deep-buy: context-conditioned bounce tables (card rsi-deep-context-tables, f4d14f093)

what.name: Event
what.value_plain: RSI14 of the TF (1m, 5m, 15m, 60m) closes at or below level L (10..40 step 5) after being 3+ above; fill = next bar open
what.label: OURS

what.name: Outcome
what.value_plain: price: open 60 min after the fill beats the fill by more than the 0.10% round-trip fee; rsi: RSI rises 5 off its running minimum before it falls 3 below entry, within 60 bars
what.label: OURS

what.name: Question
what.value_plain: does any of 21 context schemes (macro trend / vol / range terciles, trailing floors over 4h..1w) predict the bounce better than the level-only table F0?
what.label: OURS

what.name: Keep rule
what.value_plain: DEV delta log-loss > 0 with Holm p < 0.05 over all 168 tests, then VALIDATION delta > 0 (read once)
what.label: OURS

how: Walk-forward (k+1)/(n+2) per cell, shrunk to F0 by empirical Bayes (m from DEV, clamp 2..5000); t over distinct days.
window: DEV = bar open < 2024-07-01 (frozen first); VALIDATION 2024-07-01..2025-06-30 read once; HOLDOUT never read

verdict.label: NULL: 4 of 168 kept by the letter of the rule, none material; the level-only table stays

why: DEV candidates: 5 of 168. VALIDATION delta above 0 for 4 of them, but VALIDATION t over days is 0.60, 0.08, 0.60, 1.26 (none reaches 2).
The gains are a few 1e-4 nats of log-loss per event: a context that passes by the rule but changes nothing a trader could use.
Shrinkage prior m hit the 5000 clamp in 6 of 8 TF x outcome cells: the context cells are not more spread than chance around their parent.
